step2 '2. Matrixyl 3000 Serum' <- matrixyl_3000_pro_collagen_10_percent_firming_repair_skin_serum_applying_to_cheekbone_4_skingenetix.png, 2048x2048. NO BRANDING IS IN FRAME - a glass dropper and a bead of serum against skin - so there is no label to verify and nothing for an engine to have misspelled. Replaces skingenetix-howto-step2-serum.jpg, the generic stock serum shot this page shared with brightening-glow.

step3 '3. Firming Cream' <- _matrixyl_3000_triple_collagen_elastin_full_firming_face_cream_open_jar_swatch_2_skingenetix.png, 2048x2048, carrying Malcolm's underscore mark. LABEL READ AT NATIVE PIXELS, ALL SIX ELEMENTS CORRECT: the dots-and-dashes helix mark, 'Skingenetix', 'MATRIXYL 3000 PRO COLLAGEN', 'FULL & FIRMING TREATMENT', 'PREMIUM FORMULA', and 'MATRIXYL 3000 | TRIPLE COLLAGEN | ELASTIN | 50ML'. Both of this project's known failure words are right: MATRIXYL (which failed in roughly thirty of fifty candidates on one Seedream-only evening, coming back as MATPIXYL among others) and TRIPLE (recorded as TRIPPLE on the carton artwork). Neither can be judged from a contact sheet.

step4 '4. Protect' <- skingenetix-daily-spf-sunscreen-cream-application-face.jpg, ALREADY ON SHOPIFY from the brightening-glow step-4 job earlier today - the de-jarred matrixyl cheek shot. Its uploaded_handle is pre-filled here so scripts/upload-theme-images.py skips it (it filters on `not i.get('uploaded_handle')`). Re-uploading the same name would NOT replace the file: Shopify suffixes a collision and keeps serving the original, which has caught this store three times. The same picture now appears as step 4 on two pages, which is deliberate reuse rather than an oversight.

All three are 1.000:1, matching step1 at 1024x1024, so the row keeps a single shape - the fault has to be measured across the SET, because each image looks fine alone.

Outgoing files are left in Shopify Files untouched per .claude/rules/shopify.md rule 7.
